module.purpose: Provides a React hook that tracks whether a globally registered menu is open, synchronizes that state with the shared menu registry, and cleans up descendant menus when a parent unmounts.
module.summary: This file defines a public React hook for integrating menu components with a shared global menu registry. It exposes reactive open-state information and a memoized change handler, records optional menu lifecycle events, and uses effect cleanup to remove the current menu and any prefixed submenu entries when the parent closes or unmounts.
module.businessContext: Supports editor menu and submenu lifecycle management. If synchronization fails, stale menus can remain registered or parent closure may leave descendant menus open.
functions: useGlobalMenuIsOpen (~L6-63): Tracks global menu state and coordinates lifecycle cleanup.

import { useValue } from '@tldraw/state-react'
import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef } from 'react'
import { tlmenus } from '../globals/menus'

detail.name: useGlobalMenuIsOpen
detail.signature: export function useGlobalMenuIsOpen(id: string, onChange?: (isOpen: boolean) => void, onEvent?: (id: string) => void)
preconditions: id is a string identifying the menu in the global menu registry.
postconditions: Returns a readonly tuple containing the reactive boolean indicating whether id is present in tlmenus.getOpenMenus() and an onOpenChange callback.
When the returned callback is invoked, the local open-state reference matches the supplied boolean.
When the returned callback is invoked with true, id is added to the global open-menu registry; when invoked with false, id is deleted from it.
The optional onChange callback is invoked with the supplied open-state value after the global registry update.
invariants: The reactive isOpen value is determined by whether the current global open-menu list includes id.
An open menu is re-added to the global registry when the effect runs or reruns.
Cleanup only performs close processing when the menu's tracked local state is open.
During open-menu cleanup, every currently registered menu ID beginning with id is deleted.
edgeCases: If onChange is omitted, changing the menu state updates the registry without invoking a change callback.
If onEvent is omitted, lifecycle event notifications are skipped while registry synchronization still occurs.
If an effect cleanup runs while the menu is tracked as closed, it does not delete the menu or matching submenu IDs.
When cleanup runs for an open menu, it first deletes id, then deletes every remaining open-menu ID whose string starts with id and emits a close event for each such matching ID.
stateMutations: Mutates the internal rIsOpen ref with the latest callback-provided open state.
Adds or deletes menu IDs in the global tlmenus open-menu registry.
Deletes matching descendant menu IDs from the global registry during effect cleanup.
eventsEmitted: Invokes onEvent with "open-menu" when an effect runs while the menu is locally tracked as open.
Invokes onEvent with "close-menu" once for each matching open-menu ID removed during cleanup.
detail.summary: Provides reactive global-menu open state for a menu identifier and a callback that updates the global open-menu registry. It also synchronizes open submenus across effect reruns and removes the menu and matching descendant menus during cleanup.

specTests.when: The returned state-change callback is invoked with true and then false.
